title: Add typed authored relationships (requires/alternative/refutes/supersedes) distinct from plain markdown links
description:
Ordinary Markdown links come through as kind=link. Reference schemas tolerate extra frontmatter, but opaque metadata does not make a proof dependency legible to graph/path/impact.

Proposed: declared relationship types -- requires, alternative, refutes, supersedes -- with precise statement/version references, and claim outcome plus evidence level kept separate from document status and task completion.

Acceptance worth keeping as stated by the finding: a proof-only view excludes background links and alternatives, and changing a referenced version identifies affected dependents for review. Note the deliberate modesty there -- it reports possible impact, not a mathematical correctness verdict.

Source: 2026-09-13 proof-graph inspection (Lore 0.6.0, Quest 0.6.0), read-only against production, recorded as OPAG-120 on opum-agent.

acceptanceCriteria.text: At least the four named relationship kinds (requires, alternative, refutes, supersedes) are representable in frontmatter/schema, each with a precise statement/version reference
A proof-only graph/path/impact view excludes background links and alternatives, surfacing only proof-typed relationships
Claim outcome and evidence level are tracked as fields distinct from document status and task completion
Changing a referenced statement version identifies affected dependents for review, reported as possible impact rather than a correctness verdict

implementationNotes:
DELIBERATELY NOT STARTED, 2026-09-14. THIS IS A DECISION, NOT UNFINISHED WORK, and the distinction
matters to whoever picks it up: nothing here was begun and abandoned, no branch exists, no design was
half-chosen. The task is exactly as it was filed, on purpose.

THE REASONING, so it is not re-litigated or mistaken for avoidance:

LCLI-477 is the most DESIGN-SHAPED of the five items in the 0.7.0 burndown. Typed authored
relationships -- requires / alternative / refutes / supersedes -- plus keeping claim outcome and
evidence level separate from document status and task completion, is work where THE SHAPE IS THE
WORK. The implementation follows from the vocabulary; the vocabulary is the hard part and it is
close to irreversible once authored documents start using it.

It became eligible only when LCLI-476 landed: 476 and 477 both own src/core/traversal.ts and
src/core/graph.ts, so 477 could not run in parallel with it (that collision is why it was held rather
than dispatched alongside LCLI-492). With 476 merged, the collision is gone and 477 is unblocked.

It was then left unstarted because starting it at the end of a very long session is how a vocabulary
gets chosen by fatigue rather than judgement. A tired session picks the first defensible set of
relationship names and they become permanent. Better begun fresh, by a session with room to argue
with itself about the taxonomy.

opum-agent reviewed this reasoning and ACCEPTED it explicitly ("do not start it -- you are right and
the reasoning is better than the instruction"), so this is a recorded fleet decision and not one
session's preference. Do not treat 477 as dropped, and do not treat the order confirmation
(479 -> 492 -> 476 -> 478 -> 477) as having been abandoned; 477 is simply last and its start was
deferred by one session boundary.

WHAT A FRESH SESSION SHOULD KNOW BEFORE STARTING IT:

- File scope will be src/core/traversal.ts, src/core/links.ts, src/core/graph.ts (measured, not
  guessed -- these are where the `kind: "link"` edge vocabulary lives today).
- Ordinary Markdown links currently arrive as kind="link". LCLI-476 has just added a second authored
  edge kind, "dependency", emitted from tracker prerequisites with workspaceFromKind/workspaceToKind
  both "task". READ THAT IMPLEMENTATION FIRST -- it is the worked example of adding an edge kind end
  to end (projection producer, validator, traversal, rendering, and a mutation-tested guard), and 477
  is the same shape repeated for authored relationships rather than tracker-derived ones.
- Adding edge kinds did NOT require teaching traversal anything: assertKnownEdgeKinds reads the kinds
  present in the snapshot, and bounded depth and cycle handling are kind-agnostic. Expect the same,
  and verify rather than assume.
- A new authored edge vocabulary is very likely a PROJECTION SHAPE CHANGE, which means the export
  schema version question again. 476 moved it 1.0 -> 1.1 and established the pattern: write strictly
  at the current version, READ tolerantly across superseded ones (retained snapshots cannot be
  re-exported, so a strict reader destroys provenance). If 477 lands before the 0.7.0 tag it can ride
  the same 1.1; after the tag it needs 1.2. See LCLI-496 for why that window matters.
- The finding's own acceptance language is worth preserving verbatim and is deliberately MODEST: a
  proof-only view excludes background links and alternatives, and changing a referenced version
  IDENTIFIES AFFECTED DEPENDENTS FOR REVIEW. It reports possible impact, not a mathematical
  correctness verdict. Do not let the implementation over-claim what the graph can know.
finalSummary:
Delivered in PR #76, CI run 34910298959 on head ab8241b0 -- 10 checks SUCCESS, 2 SKIPPED (the promotion gates), none failed. That run validates the implementation; this closing commit adds tracker records only.

ADR-0021 records the vocabulary and the reasoning, and landed FIRST on purpose: this is the most design-shaped item in the burndown, the shape is close to irreversible once authored documents use it, and the implementation follows from the vocabulary rather than the other way round.

AC#1 -- the four named kinds are representable in frontmatter, each with a precise statement/version reference.
`relations[]` entries carry {kind, target, statement?, version?}. `kind` is closed: requires, alternative, refutes, supersedes, superseded_by. The last two are NOT new -- they are the existing reserved coupling fields under a second, more precise spelling, producing the same edge kind so a reader walking edges never has to know which the author used. `target` resolves through the SAME `resolveRef` rule the flat fields use, so an id and a relative path mean what they mean everywhere else, and an unresolvable target dangles rather than disappearing. Measured on a real bundle: `claims/theorem -requires-> claims/lemma` carrying statement "Lemma 3.2" and version "3".

A flat `requires: [ids]` field was rejected with the reason recorded: it slots into REF_FIELDS for free and cannot carry the qualifiers without encoding structure inside a string, which is the finding's own opaque-metadata defect one layer down.

AC#2 -- a proof-only view excludes background links and alternatives.
`--proof-only` on graph, path and impact selects requires/refutes/supersedes/superseded_by. `alternative` is excluded deliberately and is the member a hand-written `--edge` list gets wrong: an alternative is a relationship BETWEEN claims, not support FOR one. `superseded_by` is included although the finding named four kinds, because it is the same relation authored from the other endpoint and a view honouring one spelling but not its mirror reports a different graph depending on which side the author wrote on.

The clearest evidence is the same command twice on the same bundle:
  lore impact claims/lemma --direction inbound             -> via claims/lemma <-link- claims/theorem
  lore impact claims/lemma --direction inbound --proof-only -> via claims/lemma <-requires- claims/theorem
The first is a "see also" aside and a proof dependency rendered identically. That is the finding, in one line.

Two deliberate refusals inside this criterion. The preset is EXEMPT from assertKnownEdgeKinds -- an explicit `--edge` value the snapshot lacks is almost always a typo and is reported as one, but the same rule on a preset would turn "this bundle records no proof relations yet" into a usage error when it is the correct answer. And `--proof-only` with `--edge` is refused rather than intersected, because each expresses a complete answer to "which edge kinds" and guessing between them is how a filter silently returns less than either flag alone.

On `lore graph` the filter applies to EDGES, not nodes: a claim with no proof relationships stays in the view, because an unsupported claim is precisely what a proof view should surface rather than hide.

AC#3 -- claim outcome and evidence level are distinct from document status and task completion.
`claim_outcome`, `claim_evidence_level`, `claim_version`, reserved on every type, never derived from `status`, from `lore_task_status`, or from each other, and never written by lore. The test that proves the separation asserts a document that is `status: stable` AND `lore_task_status: done` AND `claim_outcome: open` simultaneously -- a combination that could not exist if any were derived from another.

The vocabulary says `supported` rather than `proved` and `checked` rather than `verified` on purpose: lore validates the syntax of a record and never the truth of one, and a vocabulary that says `proved` invites a documentation tool to be quoted as a proof assistant.

AC#4 -- changing a referenced version identifies affected dependents for review, as possible impact rather than a verdict.
`lore check` emits, measured:
  warning claims/theorem.md [relation-version-drift]: relations[0] requires claims/lemma (Lemma 3.2) was recorded against claim_version "3", which is now "4" -- this dependent may need review
Warn-tier on principle rather than convenience: lore can see that a cited version moved and cannot see whether the citing argument still holds. A test asserts the message contains "may need review" and matches none of /invalid|broken|wrong|incorrect/.

Only the drifted state warns, but `lore graph --json` carries `versionState` on EVERY relation edge including when nothing drifted -- current, stale, unversioned, untracked. Reporting only the drifted case would leave silence ambiguous between "compared and agreed" and "nothing was comparable", which is a marker that cannot announce its own applicability. `claim_version` is author-declared rather than content-derived because a hash moves when a typo is fixed, which would flag every dependent and train readers to ignore the signal.

`relationOrdinal` is the piece that makes the four states honest and is easy to miss: `supersedes` can arrive from a relation OR from the flat field, and only the first can record a version. Without the discriminator a flat `supersedes` would report `unversioned` -- "the author omitted it" -- when the spelling has nowhere to put one. A test asserts a flat-field edge carries no versionState at all.

ADDITIVE, PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Reserved keys are APPENDED to the canonical order, and the test pins the WHOLE order rather than a suffix so a future field inserted anywhere but the end fails. Qualifiers are omitted rather than emitted as null, so a relation-free projection produces the identical record stream and export digest. Relation edges ride projection schema 1.1 rather than forcing 1.2, because 1.1 has never shipped -- no consumer has held a 1.1 without relations, so there is nothing for a second bump to distinguish. `lore sync` against this repository rewrote no concept.

`lore rename`/`supersede` repoint `relations[].target`. A target-bearing field the rewrite engine does not know about silently dangles on the first rename, and the REF_FIELDS compile-time pin only covers refs whose whole value is the reference -- a structured field slips straight past it.

TESTS ARE MUTATION-SENSITIVE, verified rather than claimed: removing relationOrdinal fails 3; validating the preset like an --edge value fails 1; dropping the relations[].target rewrite fails 1; folding unversioned into current fails 3 across two files. The indexed/reference conformance fixture now authors two relations, one citing a stale version, because the qualifiers are SPARSE -- an indexed read that dropped them entirely would still produce edges with the right endpoints and kinds, and a whole-output comparison of two backends that both dropped them would agree with itself.

FOUND AND FIXED ALONG THE WAY, kept out of this change: LCLI-497 (merged, PR #75) -- the indexed backend was dead on any tracker with a prerequisite, found because this task needed a working indexed path to verify its own fidelity. LCLI-498 and LCLI-499 are filed and not done.

Validation: bun test 3027 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail; typecheck clean; lint clean; lore check 78 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
